issuer: the Minister responsible for transport, through the Transport Control Department (TCD)
note: Read 2026-10-30 on Bermuda Laws Online (the Attorney-General's Chambers' consolidated laws) and the Transport Control Department's page on gov.bm. The Motor Car Act 1951 (consolidated): a driver's licence is issued by the Minister to an applicant who passes a driving examination and pays the prescribed fees (s 76; private motor cars are class (h)); a driver's licence or learner's permit isn't issued to anyone under eighteen (s 80), so it is held from 18; a licence issued at eighteen or over remains in force for ten years (s 86(1)(a)), but one that would remain in force past the holder's seventieth birthday remains in force only until then (s 86(1A)), held as 10 years ending at 70 at most (untilAge); TCD's page says the same (a licence for up to ten years, or up to the 70th birthday). The Government Fees Regulations 1976 (consolidated), Head 47 (Motor Car Act 1951): issuing or renewing a ten year driver's licence not specifically provided for, $121, the fee held; the examination for a certificate of competence ($50) and the learner's permit ($27) aren't held. No identity card is held, and no exchange list was read.
